# Section

* [Sparkle rendering](about.md) - Techniques for rendering glitter, spangles and crystals in real time: glint models, crystal optics look-alike, the proposed four-level stone LOD, instancing at scale, lighting, observer/glare, tone mapping, temporal stability and validation.

# Technique

* [Coloured, iridescent and holographic glitter](coloured-and-holographic-glitter.md) - Per-flake colour (Kemppinen 2025), thin-film iridescence (Belcour-Barla 2017, glTF KHR_materials_iridescence, three.js), diffraction-grating holographic flakes (no validated real-time glint method) and car-paint flake precedents.
* [Four-level crystal LOD chain (proposed)](crystal-lod-chain.md) (draft) - The research team's own, unvalidated proposal for drawing 2,000-100,000 crystals: per-stone LOD by projected size (traced facets, table-shaded mesh, analytic quad, folded into a glint lobe) sharing one per-stone lobe set and seed so the same stone flashes at every level; precomputed per-cut exit-lobe tables.
* [Crystal optics look-alike](crystal-optics-look-alike.md) - How to shade a flat-back crystal in real time: low-index faceted dome over a mirror, unfolded into a convex polyhedron for a cheap analytic tracer in close-up, dispersion and AB thin film as presets; web gem renderers (three-mesh-bvh, drei, iJewel3D) as references; the PoC's injected inner-reflection shader.
* [Glint models for glitter](glitter-glint-models.md) - Procedural count-the-flakes-in-the-footprint glint BRDFs (Zirr-Kaplanyan 2016 to Kemppinen 2025) render glitter fabric in real time at about 0.2-1.1 ms extra per light at 1080p; methods, costs, limitations, code availability and the recommended approach.
* [Observer and glare model](observer-and-glare-model.md) - The star-shaped flare of a rhinestone is made mostly by the eye or camera, not the stone; render radiometrically to an HDR buffer, then apply a named, selectable observer preset (naked eye in arena, broadcast camera, phone photo, studio with star filter), each a documented glare kernel plus exposure and tone curve.
* [Spangle and sequin rendering](spangle-and-sequin-rendering.md) - Treat a spangle or sequin as a very large, slightly rough flake: instanced tilted discs up close, handing off to a glint lobe built from the same per-sequin tilts at distance; tilt spread is the main appearance parameter; whole areas flash together.
* [Lighting for sparkle](sparkle-lighting.md) - Sparkle depends on light size as much as on the material: use an HDRI for the smooth lobe and gem refraction plus a bounded set of explicit small area lamps (with true angular size, exposed as the user's main sparkle dial) for glints; keep all precomputation lighting-independent.
* [Sparkle prior art, reusable code and the build-or-borrow map](sparkle-prior-art-and-code.md) - Public code exists for every glitter method and for web gem refraction, but nothing combines them into thousands of editable stones on a garment; fashion CAD (CLO, Browzwear, Style3D) treats glitter and gems as render-only or 2D print effects with no stone placement. Licences and what to port.
* [Sparkle temporal stability, anti-aliasing and HDR pipeline](sparkle-temporal-stability-and-hdr.md) - Filter sub-pixel highlights at the source (widen the lobe to the pixel and time footprint, keep the energy) instead of in image space; keep sparkle out of TAA history clamping; 16-bit float HDR; threshold-free bloom before tone mapping; progressive accumulation when idle.
* [Validating sparkle by statistics against photographed swatches](sparkle-validation.md) - No measured optical data exists for leotard fabrics or stones, so accuracy is established by photographing swatches and stone grids under one small lamp at fixed angles, reproducing the set-up, and comparing sparkle statistics (spots per cm2, intensity, colour, lifetime), plus internal LOD and convergence tests.
* [Stone instancing at scale](stone-instancing-at-scale.md) - Raw instance count is not the bottleneck (10^5 stones at 32 bytes = 3.2 MB); design for 10^3-2x10^5 instances with a 32-byte edit-in-place record, cluster/GPU culling, dirty-range uploads while painting, ID-buffer picking; WebGL2, WebGPU and three.js specifics.
* [Tone mapping with Khronos PBR Neutral](tone-mapping-pbr-neutral.md) - Use the Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapper (May 2024) so fabric and stone base colours reproduce 1:1 up to about 0.8 and only highlights compress; filmic ACES/AgX wash out saturated team colours; it holds under neutral white light, so ship a colour-check lighting preset.
